raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current evaluations of Large Language Models (LLMs) report performance at the dataset or task level, revealing what a model achieves but offering little insight into the internal processing associated with its performance. We propose a task-centric framework for characterising the model-internal processing elicited by a benchmark. It combines attention- and activation-based signals with representation-based measures to characterise benchmarks spanning a continuum from retrieval-dominant to reasoning-dominant and to surface failure modes that task-level scores conceal. We evaluate 16 LLMs across 24 diverse benchmarks and conduct targeted internal-state analyses on representative models and tasks, observing systematic differences in processing between knowledge-centric and reasoning-centric tasks. We shift evaluation from asking what score a model achieves toward characterising the processing patterns associated with that score, potentially supporting more targeted benchmark selection and more informed model choice. We open source our code at https://github.com/extraordinarylab/trace-kr.
title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM

raw_summary:
Agents SDK v0.24.0-alpha.8

Highlights

  • Approve Python tool calls before they run. Review the arguments and approve or reject the call. You can remember a decision for the rest of the Session. Managed approval example
  • Connect your own model client. The native tool loop works with async Responses and Chat Completions clients, LiteLLM, AnyLLM, and custom adapters. Application-owned model clients
  • Add Realtime voice to a Session. Use a server WebSocket, connect a browser over WebRTC, or attach to an existing SIP call. Realtime connection options
  • Resume more kinds of work. Save supported pending tool requests and approvals. Request and token budgets keep the usage already spent when you restore a supported checkpoint. Restore a checkpoint with a budget
  • Install on more Linux systems. The preview adds an ARM64 wheel. Both Linux wheels support glibc 2.28 or newer. Preview wheel platform requirements

Added

  • Observe tool-search calls, tool-search results, and hosted MCP approval decisions through ModelOutputItemCompleted. Use include_execution_details=True to receive full items; receive summaries by default. Live tool observations
  • Use native Session Realtime APIs from agents.realtime.native, including RealtimeAgentConfig(is_tool_enabled=...). Keep retained Classic/v0 Realtime imports under agents.realtime. Native voice · Classic imports
  • Handle managed function approvals with FunctionToolApprovalRequest and FunctionToolApprovalDecision. Set run_input_policy_before_approval=True to run the input policy before the approval predicate as well as before execution. Return FinishTurn(output) from tool_batch_completion to propose a final value with output validation and completion checks. Managed approvals · Finish a tool batch
  • Create a remote conversation only when needed with ConversationsHistory.ensure_conversation_id(). Preserve a checked history prefix with Session.replace_history_suffix(keep_prefix_count=...), and append staged checkpoint input with SessionState.with_appended_pending_input(). Read Unix milliseconds from StoredTurn.started_at_ms and completed_at_ms. History APIs · History edits
  • Use SQLAlchemySQLiteSessionStore for an application-owned synchronous SQLite engine, and ResponsesSocketFactoryOptions for resolved WebSocket connection parameters. Read received logprob data through TextLogprobsFact, TokenLogprob, TokenLogprobAlternative, and MalformedLogprobsFact, with unchanged serialized record kinds. Import ModelRunOwner from agents.models and ApplicationToolOutput from agents.state. SQLite storage · Model ownership and socket options · Logprob facts
  • Group prompt-cache routing for fresh Sessions with an explicit TraceOptions.group_id. Keep the saved cache key when restoring a Session. Set a borrowed model adapter's prompt_cache_key to override only that adapter's outgoing key. Treat routing as affinity without a guaranteed cache hit. Prompt-cache routing
  • Route work through native handoffs or call a specialist with Agent.as_tool(). Add input and output guardrails, or use Agent.decide() for a separate typed decision with explicit input. Handoffs · Typed decisions
  • Use standalone Python function tools and select MCP tools by alias. Defer eligible tool schemas with ToolSearch. Function tools also support strict schemas, output schemas, and an option to ignore extra arguments. Python tool declarations · Tool schema discovery
  • Use Redis, MongoDB, SQLAlchemy, or a Dapr Redis state component to store supported root conversations through CustomStorage. Compatible Responses providers also support provider-managed conversation history. Application-owned storage
  • Use ordinary manual FunctionTool requests and preapproved HttpMCP tools with CustomStorage. Suspend a supported manual request and restore into independent memory. To continue through the original backend, use an unchanged checkpoint with one unresolved ordinary manual call. Keep managed function approvals, pending MCP requests, and staged input outside that same-backend restore path. CustomStorage support and checkpoint limits
  • Open read-only execution environments, supply skills, or implement command and patch tools with application callbacks. Callbacks run with the application's permissions. Read-only workspaces · Native skills
  • Set per-request model options for sampling, retries, deadlines, and prompt caching. Request produced items and history from one-shot runs, or opt in to provider reasoning summaries and tool-argument deltas. Model request controls · Streaming and retained history

Changed

  • Native streaming HTTP can negotiate HTTP/2. Buffered Responses continue to use HTTP/1.1.
  • Set NativeProvider(tool_output_token_limit=...) to adjust the approximate tool-result budget for model context. Leave it unset to use the model's default. The setting is separate from the final answer limit. Tool output limit reference

Fixed

  • Reject invalid web-starter request bodies and prompts before admitting work. Reject deeply nested JSON, non-object bodies, and text without valid UTF-8 encoding. Web-starter request validation
  • Wait for confirmed remote command exit during cancellation. Report a failure when the executor acknowledges a stop without confirming exit.
  • Preserve the backing store's configured history limit when a Classic compaction wrapper has no explicit settings. Explicit wrapper and per-run limits still take precedence.
  • Strict Python tools return a retryable error to the model when the original arguments fail validation, before approval or callback execution. A corrected call still goes through approval when required. Function argument validation reference
  • Preserve completed tool results during supported checkpoint restores. Report uncertain calls for reconciliation before reopening local profiles with interrupted child work. Recover after an interruption
  • Preserve accepted model settings and history across supported handoffs and retries. Improve provider error reporting so applications can see where a request failed. Inspect provider response attempts
  • Harden protection for native workspace metadata and credential files. Reduce startup work for simple runs and reuse eligible HTTP connections.

Upgrading from 0.24.0-alpha.7

  • Use the alpha.8 wheel for the features in these notes. Some linked guides still refer to development builds. If an example needs files from the repository, use the revision linked in these notes. Alpha.7 does not accept newer keywords such as strict on function_tool or model_backend on NativeProvider.
  • For Linux local execution, install bubblewrap with a compatible bwrap in /usr/bin or /bin and allow sandbox namespace creation. For a Linux Docker executor, supply bwrap in the container image or executor bundle. Linux executor setup
  • Back up your saved state before upgrading. Alpha.7 supports budgets for live runs. Alpha.8 adds checkpointing for supported pending runs with request or token budgets. The checkpoint saves the requests or tokens already used so they still count after restore. Alpha.7 rejects this new format because it cannot enforce the saved budget. We verified that both versions can reopen idle checkpoints, checkpoints waiting for a manual Python tool reply, and closed LocalStorage profiles on Linux x86-64. These checks used matching app settings and features available in both versions. If alpha.7 cannot reopen your saved state after rollback, restore your pre-upgrade backup. Resume a budgeted checkpoint · Checkpoint restore setup · Reopen a local profile
  • Replace bare "*" entries in network domain rules with exact hosts or scoped patterns such as "*.example.org". To allow outbound public hosts, use NetworkPolicy.allow_all(). On Linux, this also requires allow_all_unix_sockets=True and an executor isolated from host services and other jobs. Explicit network policies remain unsupported on Windows. Network policy and platform limits
  • If you relied on a saved Codex login to enable ChatGPT Apps tools, add the existing ChatGPTAppsMCP declaration to the Agent's tools. Supply the provisioned Apps token, its account ID, and the tool names you want to expose. A saved Codex login now supplies model authentication only. ChatGPT Apps setup
  • If your code reads session.items(), count each execution once. Provider function_call and function_call_output rows can accompany a typed record for the same execution. Match native thread_id, turn_id, and call_id rather than counting rows or relying on a history cursor's id. Recheck saved-history readers and analytics before upgrading. Execution history
  • If you use Classic WorkspaceJsonlSink, choose a log budget before upgrading. Its default is now 8 MiB. Exceeding the existing-file or pending-buffer budget drops pending events and permanently stops that sink; rebinding does not restart it. Create a new sink for a new outbox or a larger finite max_bytes, or use JsonlOutboxSink or HttpProxySink outside the workspace for long-lived logs. Use max_bytes=None only for trusted workloads that need unlimited reads. The sink does not rotate or truncate logs. Workspace sink limits
  • If you use the classic-blaxel extra and pin Blaxel, update the pin to 0.2.51 or newer. Test saved sandbox restoration with your current network and port settings. Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Modal, and Vercel can now reject saved settings that conflict with the current policy. Create a fresh sandbox with the required settings instead of relaxing the policy to reuse old state. Blaxel dependency · Example restore-policy check

Release verification

Source: d6a81c997eabdc56108633eb3132fb3907f87d7e.

Built and tested by Tests #43800450653.

Verified fresh installs on all four platforms with CPython 3.10 and 3.14. Installation checks

analysis.summary_cn: LuthorSQL 提出非自回归 7B Text-to-SQL 模型，单次前向预测查询计划槽位分数并运行候选计划，作为慢速 LLM Agent 的 System 1 门控，仅在不确定时升级到 Opus。BIRD 隐藏测试集执行准确率 68.03%，单 GPU 0.84 秒，8 位量化仅需 9GB，零样本迁移多数据库，配合置信级联可本地处理近半问题并降 API 成本 33.3%。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17780v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier LLM agents that query databases with tools are among the most accurate text-to-SQL systems, but per-query calls to a hosted model are slow, costly, and expose sensitive organizational queries to external APIs. For example, a Claude Opus 5.5 agent serving 10,000 queries a day costs over $70,000 a year at list price. To what extent can local hardware already owned by an organization offload this burden without compromising the agent's accuracy? We present LuthorSQL, a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that serves as a rapid System 1 gate for a slower LLM agent (System 2), escalating queries only when uncertain. LuthorSQL makes a single forward pass to predict slot scores over a bounded grammar for query plans, compiles and runs up to 32 candidate plans, and chooses an answer using a trained validator. On its own, LuthorSQL reaches 68.03% execution accuracy on BIRD's hidden test set at 0.84 s per question on a single GPU, maintains its accuracy in 9 GB with 8-bit quantized weights, and transfers zero-shot to Snowflake, BigQuery, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and DuckDB within 3.1 points of its native SQLite accuracy. Combined with Claude Opus 5.5 in a pre-registered confidence cascade over 227 questions on databases published after Opus's training cutoff, LuthorSQL answers nearly half of all questions locally and cuts API cost by 33.3% at the same accuracy. Finally, contamination probing shows that Opus reproduces 48-92% of public benchmark gold queries verbatim without seeing the schema; however, its tool-assisted accuracy holds on renamed schemas and reaches 95.6-97.4% on post-cutoff databases. Code and data: https://github.com/IAMIbrahimmemon/luthorsql
title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent

analysis.action: 可入库并关注，建议阅读全文评估实验设置与可复现性
analysis.reason: 来自 arXiv 官方，可信度较高；主题契合用户关注的 RAG 与 Agent 方向，针对生成式检索中查询改写优化这一核心环节提出新框架，具备一定参考价值，但尚未见开源实现或社区验证。
analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 新论文提出 RAG-FGO，用于生成式 RAG 中查询改写策略的动态优化。它将查询改写建模为混合离散-连续空间的黑盒优化问题，把提示模板与解码参数视为可自适应优化的改写智能体，通过全局搜索跳出局部最优、局部扰动精细对齐，并用精英保留记忆池累积优质策略以缓解噪声反馈。多基准实验显示有效且稳健。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17788v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), query rewriting serves as a core interface that aligns user intent with external knowledge bases, and its effectiveness directly determines overall system performance. However, generative retrieval faces three critical challenges in real-world deployment: noisy retrieval feedback, the difficulty of jointly optimizing discrete prompt templates and continuous decoding-control parameters, and the limited generalization of static rewriting strategies under semantically complex scenarios. To address these issues, we propose RAG-FGO, a dynamic optimization framework for generative retrieval strategies. RAG-FGO formulates query rewriting as a non-differentiable black-box optimization problem in a mixed discrete-continuous space, and represents prompt templates and decoding parameters as adaptively optimizable query-rewriting agents. The framework performs global search to enable semantic jumps and structural reorganization that escape local optima, while applying local perturbations for fine-grained alignment and precise refinement. In addition, RAG-FGO introduces an elite-preserving memory pool that accumulates high-quality strategies across iterations, thereby mitigating the impact of stochasticity and noisy feedback on optimization stability. Experimental results on a diverse suite of benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, supporting its applicability to complex semantic retrieval tasks.
title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG

analysis.action: 精读论文并复现代码/评测设置，评估其上下文选择器能否迁移到自有 Agent 流水线
analysis.reason: 直击长程 Agent 上下文膨胀痛点，提出学习型保留策略且无需额外 LLM 调用，多项基准稳定超越基线，并补充成本-成功率评测指标；与用户 Agent、Eval 偏好高度契合，来源为 arXiv 一手论文可信度高。
analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 论文提出 CarryOn，一种轻量级长期任务 LLM Agent 上下文管理器。它用紧凑的执行状态加细粒度、可追溯来源的证据，并配学习型选择器与自适应保留策略，无需额外 LLM 调用即可管理上下文。在 AppWorld、OfficeBench、Tau2 Telecom 三个基准、三种 LLM Actor 上，宏平均任务成功率达 75.7%，超最强基线 6.7 个百分点，并新提出 S_α 与 NCS 两项兼顾成本与成功的指标。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17808v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents can coordinate tools and applications to complete complex, multi-step tasks. As their interaction histories grow, effective context management becomes essential for reliable and efficient execution. Existing methods reduce context through summarization, pruning, or history selection. However, shorter contexts do not necessarily support better decisions: summaries can omit exact details needed for later actions, while retaining entire interactions can carry substantial irrelevant information. We propose CarryOn, a lightweight context manager that pairs compact execution state with fine-grained, source-linked evidence. A learned selector and adaptive retention policy keep relevant evidence available without additional LLM calls for context management. We introduce two complementary evaluation metrics: $S_\alpha$ prioritizes task success while accounting for resource use, and normalized cost per success (NCS) measures the resources spent per successful task. Across AppWorld, OfficeBench, and Tau2 Telecom with three LLM Actors, CarryOn achieves 75.7% macro-averaged task success, exceeding the strongest baseline by 6.7 percentage points. It also achieves the best average scores on both metrics.
title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

analysis.action: read
analysis.reason: 来自arXiv官方来源，可信度高；聚焦Agent记忆过滤与RAG检索可靠性，与用户对Agent/Eval/RAG的偏好高度相关。研究揭示了记忆删除的误删风险及门控策略，对构建可靠Agent记忆系统有直接工程指导价值，值得精读。
analysis.summary_cn: 该arXiv论文研究LLM记忆系统中的删除过滤问题：当解析器错误地把查询关键事实判为过时并硬删除时，下游准确率会从完美解析时的+0.19~+0.23增益转为最低可靠性下的-0.18损失。误删比误留危害更大，非删除基线在错误标签误导生成时仍会失败。在102/102校准-测试划分上，部署匹配门控达0.655准确率，高于始终硬删的0.641。作者建议将删除视为代价敏感决策，缺乏验证时默认保留。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17338v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM memory systems often delete facts classified as stale. We show that this hard-filtering step can reduce downstream accuracy when resolver errors delete query-critical facts. Across three models, a controlled sensitivity intervention moves hard-drop from gains of +0.186 to +0.230 at perfect resolution to losses of -0.176 to -0.181 at the lowest tested reliability. Paired targeted interventions show that false-drop causes significantly greater degradation than false-keep, while a non-deleting baseline can still fail when incorrect labels steer generation. On a frozen 102/102 calibration/test split, a simple deployment-matched gate reaches 0.655 accuracy versus 0.641 for always hard-drop and 0.662 for test-informed oracle selection. Global-accuracy crossovers require gold labels and are model- and task-specific diagnostics, not deployment thresholds. Deletion should instead be treated as cost-sensitive: validate query-critical false-drop risk on matched data, or default to label-free retention when such validation is unavailable.
title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors

analysis.action: read
analysis.reason: 对RAG检索对象设计有直接启示：将患者级近邻检索替换为任务对齐的人群统计先验，在固定词表结构化预测上稳定提升且零额外LLM开销，属于RAG+Eval方向的可复现改进，值得精读方法与消融细节。
analysis.summary_cn: 该论文指出临床RAG常把EHR用药预测当作开放案例推理，而实际目标是固定词表的离散集合预测。作者提出用训练集统计的条件-药物共现表构建表格化人群先验，作为更对齐任务的检索对象，替换PACERAG的患者检索器后，F1从0.303升至0.338（相对+11.5%），Jaccard从0.218升至0.237，无需额外LLM调用和推理期患者索引。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17341v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medication prediction from electronic health records is a fixed vocabulary structured prediction problem, yet recent clinical RAG systems often treat it like open ended case based reasoning: retrieve similar patient admissions and ask an LLM to infer a medication set. This retrieval object is indirect the model receives retrieved patient records while the target is a discrete set of medication class labels. We propose a more task aligned retrieval object: a tabular population prior ranked medication class candidates from a sparse condition medication co occurrence table estimated from training admissions. Using PACERAG as a fixed downstream pipeline and replacing only its patient retriever, this drop in swap improves F1 from 0.303 to 0.338 (+11.5% relative) and Jaccard from 0.218 to 0.237 on 1,004 heldout MIMIC IV admissions, with no additional LLM calls and no inference time patient index. A non LLM top k baseline reaches F1=0.248, confirming the prior is predictive before LLM integration. Aggregate population statistics can provide a more task aligned, efficient, and auditable retrieval source than patient level nearest neighbors for fixed vocabulary EHR set prediction.
title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction

analysis.summary_cn: 本文把粉末X射线衍射(pXRD)结构解析建模为可验证的Agent搜索问题：推理时用前向模拟谱吻合度评估候选结构，评测时用结构匹配。提出pXRD-Bench含200个模拟单相问题，Agent适配使结构恢复率从27%升至69%，验证器引导的推理时扩展进一步提升；并扩展到实验多相数据，用自生成合成问题训练进化Agent与可执行工具，15个实测谱上提升谱吻合度，还能恢复参考库缺失的相。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17539v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous crystal-structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction (pXRD) remains a key bottleneck for self-driving materials laboratories. We formulate the task of pXRD structure determination as a verifiable agentic search problem: candidate structures can be assessed during inference through forward-simulated profile agreement and during evaluation through structural matching to a known reference. To benchmark progress, we introduce pXRD-Bench, a suite of 200 simulated single-phase problems spanning in-distribution structure determination, challenging and polymorphic structures, and controlled compositional and topological distribution shifts. Agent adaptation raises selected structural recovery from 27% to 69%, with further gains from repeated sampling and verifier-guided inference-time scaling. We extend this approach to experimental multiphase pXRD through a reflexive evolution framework that learns from self-generated synthetic problems. A replaceable laboratory specification defines the sample family and measurement conditions. An evolver agent uses the known generating structures and measurement parameters to diagnose solver failures and develop persistent guidance and executable tools, which are then provided to agents on measured patterns. This supplies verifiable training experience without requiring a collection of solved experimental measurements. On 15 measured patterns from solid-state synthesis, the evolved package improves average profile agreement and transfers an analogue-substitution procedure that recovers a phase whose structure is absent from the supplied reference library. These results demonstrate how learning from verifiable synthetic experience can improve agentic characterization of experimental samples whose structures are not known in advance.
title: Verifiable pXRD: Hill-climbing pXRD structure determination with LLM agents

raw_summary:
Qwen4-Max from Alibaba is now available on AI Gateway. It is the first model in the Qwen4 series: a reasoning model with native vision and a 1M-token context window, built for coding, professional work, and long-running agent tasks.

Qwen4-Max is better at working with professional tools. It can build 3D scenes in Blender and playable games in Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot, running what it builds and using visual feedback to fix camera, animation, and lighting issues. For finance, legal, and healthcare work, it can call many MCP tools, work through large sets of documents and images, and produce spreadsheets, slide decks, and reports that cite their sources.

For long-running tasks, the model delivers a usable first version early and then improves it in successive releases, so you can review progress and change direction before the work is finished. Alibaba is open-sourcing a Live Delivery plugin for this workflow. Compared with prior Qwen Max models, Qwen4-Max uses fewer tokens to complete the same tasks and writes more secure code by default, with fewer injection, memory safety, and access control vulnerabilities.

Use alibaba/qwen4-max as the model name:

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest Vercel CLI and run setup:

analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 新论文提出 GDP_xlsx 基准，包含 13 个领域专业人士撰写的 70 个真实办公请求，每个请求配有专家二元评分标准和完整工作簿或 CSV（共 218 万单元格、791 条标准）。Agent 在容器中用表格工具作答，由可打开文件的 agentic judge 按标准评分，强调完整性（不能漏）与排他性（不能多）。在 20 个含 Google、Anthropic、OpenAI 前沿模型的配置中，最高分 Gemini 4 Argon 严格 pass@1 仅 38.3%，中位数 19.3%，提升空间大。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17766v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce GDP_xlsx, a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace requests written by professionals in 13 domains, each paired with an expert rubric of binary criteria and with the complete workbook or CSV file it refers to. Together the files hold 2.18 million populated cells, and the rubrics 791 criteria. Agents work in a container with spreadsheet tools, and an agentic judge that can open the file applies the rubric. Completeness and exclusivity criteria require set-valued answers to be found in full and with nothing extra. We rank models by strict pass@1, the share of attempts that meet every criterion. Across 20 model configurations, including frontier models from Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI, the top-scoring one, Gemini 4 Argon, passes only 38.3% of attempts, and the median score is 19.3%, leaving wide headroom. We release the evaluation harness and three public tasks; the other 67 are held out to protect the leaderboard from contamination.
title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks

analysis.summary_cn: 论文针对掩码扩散语言模型（MDLM）后训练中块级 ELBO 估计的方差问题，提出全块估计器：对每个块恰好评估一次再平均，理论证明其保持无偏且消除块选择带来的组间方差，同等样本量下方差更低。在数学、规划、编码五个基准上，该方法在四个基准取得最高准确率，较随机块采样基线平均提升 12.79 分。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17754v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Policy gradient methods are widely used to align large language model outputs with human preferences, but the log-likelihoods they require cannot be directly computed in Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs). MDLM post-training therefore relies on a surrogate objective based on the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), and recent work estimates a blockwise variant of this objective via Monte Carlo methods to support blockwise generation. However, existing estimation schemes randomly sample the block index, so they may evaluate the same block more than once and leave some blocks unevaluated. This introduces variance arising from block selection into the estimates. In this work, we propose a full-block estimator that evaluates every block exactly once and averages the results. We theoretically show that the proposed estimator remains unbiased while eliminating the between-group variance arising from block selection, thereby achieving lower variance than the baseline for the same sample size. In experiments on five benchmarks spanning mathematics, planning, and coding, our method achieves the highest accuracy on four benchmarks and outperforms the random block sampling baseline by an average of 12.79 points.
title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models

analysis.reason: 来自 arXiv 的正式论文，方法与实验细节完整，可信度高；提出自蒸馏式的退火训练流程，对数据高效训练与鲁棒性有参考价值，但与 Agent、RAG、Coding、Eval 等偏好方向关联较弱，故重要性中等，建议阅读。
analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 论文提出「模型退火」训练法：在训练预算内，让模型反复升温再冷却，每个冷却状态加入过往模型预测的记忆库，并学习记忆的软化预测与对抗性「梦境」，无需额外推理开销。在 CIFAR-100 等数据集上，AdamW 训练的 ConvNeXt、ViT、MLP-Mixer 在 33 种配置中的 28 种优于交叉熵训练，平均提升 1.3 个点，并在校准与鲁棒性上表现更优。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17524v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A small labelled dataset is memorized long before the training budget runs out, and the one-hot labels that remain to be fitted then mostly sharpen confidence. Model annealing spends the rest of the budget on review and consolidation, relearning from the network's own knowledge. Training is divided into episodes whose learning rate is raised again and cooled, every cooled state joins a memory of past selves, and each new episode learns from the labels, from the tempered predictions of this memory, and from adversarial dreams sought where student and memory disagree most. The memory averages predictions rather than weights, and the deployed network is the last student, so inference costs nothing extra. Across CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet and Imagewoof, four architecture families and 5\% to 100\% of the labels, model annealing raises the top-1 accuracy of the AdamW-trained ConvNeXt, ViT and MLP-Mixer over cross-entropy training in 28 of 33 configurations, by 1.3 points on average, and is on par in accuracy with snapshot distillation, the closest competitor. On these families it is better than both in likelihood, calibration and robustness to corruptions and small adversarial perturbations. For an SGD-trained ResNet-18 it lowers accuracy but still improves robustness to small adversarial perturbations. Separating the reheated schedule from relearning shows that relearning helps every family and that the losses come from reheats, which undo most of this network's fit to its training set. How early the accuracy of a cross-entropy run saturates largely separates the AdamW families from ResNet-18 but does not predict the gain within them. With little data, relearning from the latest snapshot without dreams, as snapshot distillation does, compounds overconfidence in the AdamW families from episode to episode. The memory and the dreams each curb most of this drift, and together they remove it.
title: Model Annealing: Data-Efficient Learning through Review and Consolidation

analysis.summary_cn: 该 arXiv 论文提出用 LLM 直接对行为聚类做生命周期决策（分裂、合并、退役、新建或不动），无需重新聚类；依据标签区分度低时用统计、高时用统计+语义的固定策略。在 YooChoose、MOOC、News 三个数据集上，策略选出的 LLM 模式 F1 均最高，干预更少、更克制，优于阈值启发式与 MONIC 基线。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17616v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Behavioral clusters learned over user or item interactions drift as behavior evolves: some fragment into sub-behaviors, some converge, some disappear, and new patterns emerge. Two paradigms dominate the maintenance of evolving clusterings. Threshold triggers fire a pre-specified action when a hardcoded statistic crosses a cutoff; refit-and-track (MONIC-style) re-clusters every window and infers transitions from how the new clusters align with the previous window's. Both hardwire the decision into a threshold or a re-clustering rule. We study an alternative in which a large language model (LLM) makes the lifecycle decision in place. Given a threshold-free, whole-population view of the current cluster set (statistical health, labels, member texts, residual mass), the LLM decides per cluster whether and how to act (split, merge, retire, create, or no-action) without re-clustering. Because the useful signal channel depends on how informative the labels are, we fix a richness-conditioned policy in advance: statistics when label distinctiveness is low, fused statistics+semantics when it is high. On three public datasets spanning label richness (YooChoose 0.17, MOOC 0.50, News-Category 0.70), the policy-selected LLM mode obtains the highest F1 on all three, with far fewer interventions and stronger restraint than tuned threshold heuristics and a MONIC steelman (paired Wilcoxon p <= 0.003, bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero). The gain is concentrated more in precision than recall. The useful modality shifts from statistics to semantics/fusion as richness rises. Semantics hurt on YooChoose, fusion is roughly neutral on MOOC, and the semantic channel is required on News. One base prompt template and one fixed policy serve all three datasets, whereas the tuned baseline collapses when moved between them. We treat this shift as a practitioner diagnostic observed on three datasets, not a validated law.
title: LLM-Guided Cluster Lifecycle Management: Deciding When and How to Evolve Behavioral Clusters

Release: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0

The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap, the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub.)

I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2:

Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have

"Be creative and think outside the box" resulted in a few neat ideas - my favorite is that it displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes, then loads a WebGL preview only when they scroll into view.

I also had Claude build a comprehensive demo which works in the latest Datasette Lite, so you can visit this link to load the plugin and a demo database in your browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly.

analysis.summary_cn: arXiv 论文以四状态世界为有限模型，穷举所有合法表示与二元动作规则，精确比较“表示保留的世界信息量”与“任务收益/准确率”的关系。结果显示：保留更少信息的表示有时收益更高，有时更低，甚至信息量不同但收益相等；低信息优势取决于保留了哪些区分，并受动作约束、计数规则与成本假设影响。作者强调这只是可复现的教学式模型，用于展示信息量与决策价值的既有区分，而非提出新定律。

raw_summary:
arXiv:2611.17583v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A representation that retains one bit about a four-state world can solve a task perfectly, while another that retains 1.5 bits on average reaches only 75% accuracy. The difference lies in which distinctions each representation preserves. We examine this relationship in a uniform four-state world by enumerating all admissible representations and binary action rules. Constructions are compared both by replacing one component while holding the others fixed and by choosing the best action rule separately for each module. We consider three tasks, their mixtures, and four separate hypothetical cost tariffs.
  In some comparisons, the representation retaining less world information has the higher payoff; in others, the more informative representation does. There are also pairs with different information amounts but equal payoff--that is, equal task accuracy. If a representation preserves all existing distinctions and adds new ones, its best zero-cost payoff cannot decrease. Lower-information advantages therefore depend on which distinctions are retained. Equal counts of opposing advantages under representation replacement follow from coding symmetry. In broader comparisons, the shares depend on how repeated realizations are counted. A different task set or resource price can change which member of a fixed pair performs better.
  These results are exact, complete censuses of the specified finite sets of constructions and comparisons. The atlas provides a reproducible worked model for examining how action constraints, counting rules, and cost assumptions affect comparisons. It illustrates established distinctions between information quantity and decision value rather than proposing a new general law of their relation. $I(W;R)$ measures retained world information, and payoff measures task accuracy.
title: When Does Less Information Pay? An Exact Finite Atlas of Representation, Payoff, and Cost
